newsitem.title: FRANCE: Chirac, Kohl pledge to work together on EMU.
newsitem.headline: Chirac, Kohl pledge to work together on EMU.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac and German Chancellor Helmut Kohl are determined to work together to ensure the success of a Franco-German summit next Monday and an EU summit in Dublin later this month, an official at Chirac's office said on Tuesday.
The official was briefing reporters after nearly three hours of talks between the two leaders, which were interrupted by news of a bomb attack in a Paris underground railway train.
Chirac and Kohl had been expected to make a joint statement after their talks but called this off, leaving Chirac to make a declaration on the bombing which killed two people.

The official said that the two leaders discussed the European Union's ongoing Intergovernmental Conference as well as European monetary union issues, due to be discussed at the EU's Dublin summit later this month.
"On all these subjects the president of the republic and the chancellor are determined to do everything together to ensure the success of the Nuremberg and Dublin meetings," he told reporters.
The Franco-German summit on Monday is to be held in Nuremberg, Germany.
The official declined specific comment on whether Chirac and Kohl had reached any understanding on a proposed EU budget discipline pact.
EU finance ministers failed to agree on the so-called stability pact in talks in Brussels on Monday but are due to reconvene in Dublin on the eve of the EU summit to be held on December 13-14.
